abstract: Importance: There is usually a delay of several years before people with psychosis are identified as showing treatment resistance (TR), as this depends on careful evaluation of 2 or more courses of antipsychotic treatment; however, earlier identification could facilitate timely access to clozapine, the only approved treatment for TR psychosis. Objective: To examine whether clinical data collected when individuals first present with psychosis can be used to predict the subsequent emergence of TR. Design, Setting, and Participants: This prognostic model development and validation study used electronic health record (EHR) data from 10 mental health National Health Service trusts in the Akrivia Health database. All individuals with a first episode of psychosis (FEP) diagnosed between March 1998 and December 2014 were identified, with follow-up through December 2022. EHRs from this cohort were examined for up to 8 years following FEP diagnosis. A nested cross-validation strategy using a leave-one-trust-out approach was used for within-network external validation. Data were analyzed from February 2025 through August 2026. Exposures: A total of 179 predictors from EHR data collected at first presentation, including symptoms, sociodemographic variables, psychiatric comorbidity, and psychotropic medications. Main Outcomes and Measures: Clozapine initiation within 8 years of diagnosis was used as a proxy for TR. Penalized logistic regression was used to model associations between baseline variables and subsequent clozapine treatment. Secondary analyses examined more inclusive criteria for TR, defined as receipt of clozapine or 3 or more nonclozapine antipsychotics. Results: A total of 25 665 patients were included (mean [SD] age at FEP onset, 25.51 [5.54] years; 12 007 female [46.8%]). In the 8 years following diagnosis, 2133 patients (8.3%) had received clozapine. The model showed acceptable discrimination for clozapine initiation across trusts (mean leave-one-trust-out C statistic, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.68-0.75; positive predictive value, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.12-0.17; negative predictive value, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.95-0.97). Using more inclusive criteria, TR in FEP could still be predicted but with reduced discrimination (mean leave-one-trust-out C statistic, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.64-0.72; positive predictive value, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.24-0.31; negative predictive value, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.88-0.91). Conclusions and Relevance: Findings in this prognostic study indicate it may be possible to predict whether individuals who have just developed psychosis will subsequently show TR using clinical data collected at first presentation. This could facilitate earlier access to clozapine in the subgroup of people with psychosis in whom it is indicated.

title: Predicting Treatment Resistance in First-Episode Psychosis Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data
